title: RetentionFloorCalibration
description: One measurement per (text kind, format) of the retention floor a parser must clear before it may run. Version 2.0 exists because version 1.0 could express a lie the first real mint told: it sealed a 400-document stride-sample statistic in a field named `observedMinimum` and a release carried it as the population minimum (Decision 0001, amendment B5). This format cannot express that. There is no field named `sample` anywhere in it; `population.coverage` is the constant `full-population`; `population.measuredCount` must equal `population.documentCount`; and `observedMinimum` must equal `distribution.minimum` over that same count. A receipt that measured a sample is not writable here.

measurements.description: One per (textKind, formatKey), sorted by that pair. A format nobody measured has no floor and is refused: this array is the whole vocabulary of what may be extracted.

fraction.description: A decimal string strictly between 0 and 1, with no trailing zero. Binary floating point is refused outright by this platform's canonicaliser, and a floor written into a release must survive the round trip it will be read back through.

metric.description: What the ratio measures, stated once for the whole receipt so no measurement can quietly use another. Both sides are normalized by the same rule: the HTML extractor lays out verbatim and the XML extractor lays out normalized, so an un-normalized numerator makes the two incommensurable and produces ratios above 1.0 on real documents.

population.description: The named corpus this floor was measured on, in full. It must be DISJOINT from the corpus the floor gates -- a floor calibrated on the population it gates cannot refuse anything in it -- and the disjointness is measured rather than asserted: both are content-addressed, and `disjointness` records the overlap that was counted.

root.description: Path relative to the corpora root, so the receipt names no filesystem.

coverage.description: Constant. There is exactly one legal coverage for a calibration: the whole named population. A sample has no spelling in this format.

measuredCount.description: Equal to `documentCount`, or the measurement did not cover the population.

inventoryDigest.description: Digest over the population's sorted `{documentId, sha256, byteSize}` inventory, so the same population is re-identifiable without carrying every document into the receipt.

disjointness.description: Measured overlap with the corpus this floor gates, two ways. A digest check alone would miss the same document retrieved twice into different bytes, so the source document identifiers are intersected as well. Both must be zero, or the overlapping documents are dropped from the calibration before the floor is derived.

lowestDocument.description: The one document that set `observedMinimum`, named so the margin can be re-argued.

observedMinimum.description: Equal to `distribution.minimum`, over `population.documentCount` documents. The field name is the claim, and this format makes the claim checkable rather than trusted.

documents.description: Every document measured, one row each -- the whole named population, never a sample. `population.measuredCount` must equal this array's length, so the full-population claim is countable from the receipt rather than trusted.

measuredDocument.description: One measured document, with BOTH ratios. The gate keys on `retention` alone; `rawRetention` is kept because normalization hides exactly one thin-parse mode -- content whose meaning is carried BY its whitespace, destroyed by a parse that keeps the characters and drops the layout. A cratered raw ratio under a healthy normalized one is that signature, and nothing else in this format reports it.
